events.content: STRATEGY: ASSERT. The room just opened. The first thing on my mind is the PSI reading I saw this morning. It's unhealthy, and that directly affects my family, especially my mother with her asthma. I'll start by stating this fact and my concern. It's what's most real to me right now.
Here we go again. I just checked, the PSI is in the unhealthy range this morning. Already worried about my mother.
I've stated my initial concern and am waiting to hear from the others.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Kelvin in Singapore is worried about his mother because of the haze. It's bad here in Johor too. My main concern is my son. If his school closes, I don't know what I'll do about work.
Same here in Johor. The sky is so grey. I'm just hoping my son's school doesn't close.
Shared my primary concern.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Kelvin and Farhana are worried about the haze in Singapore and Malaysia. I understand, but the situation is much worse for my sister in Kalimantan. I should tell them what's really happening at the source of the fires. My family is suffering directly.
My sister is in Palangka Raya. In Kalimantan. She says the sky has been orange for weeks. Her children are coughing.
Waiting to see how they respond to the situation in Kalimantan.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. I want to share my own experience with school closures to show how the haze is already disrupting our lives, which connects to what Farhana and Budi said. Hearing about children coughing is really worrying and it makes my priority of keeping my daughter healthy feel more urgent.
That's awful, Budi. My daughter's school was already closed for two days this week. We had home-based learning.
Shared my experience and waiting to see how others react.

It is now Friday 18 September 2026. Air quality is unhealthy at half of Malaysia's 68 monitoring stations, and the haze reached southern Vietnam on 14 September. Malaysia has offered Indonesia one firefighting plane, three helicopters and 52 personnel. Japan has sent military helicopters to help Indonesia fight the fires. Indonesian police say 95 companies are being investigated over the fires, along with many individuals. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. It's been two weeks and things haven't gotten better. I'll share how it's been affecting me personally, especially my work. The news about investigations and international help is one thing, but the reality on the ground for me is just dealing with the bad air every day. My job is partly outdoors, so I've really been feeling it.
Two weeks... it's been terrible. I work partly outdoors and some days I can really feel it in my throat.
I've shared my experience over the last two weeks and am waiting for others to speak.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Kelvin is feeling the physical effects of the haze. It's been tough for my family too. My son's school was closed, and that's my biggest worry. I had to take leave from my job at the factory. It's a real struggle to balance everything.
It's been so bad. My son's school was closed two days last week. I had to take emergency leave from work to look after him.
Shared my recent experience with school closures.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Farhana and Kelvin are talking about their problems, like schools being closed and sore throats. I understand that, I'm a driver, I'm outside all day in Jakarta. But they don't seem to get how much worse it is for my sister in Kalimantan. It's not just an inconvenience there, it's a real health crisis. I need to make them understand the difference.
I'm on my motorbike all day, so I feel it. But my sister... It's not just about schools closing. They are afraid to go outside. The air is dangerous.
I've made my point about the severity of the situation in Kalimantan.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi is right, it's more than just an inconvenience. He's talking about real danger, which is exactly what I'm worried about for my daughter. I want to agree with him and show that I'm also taking it seriously.
Yes, exactly. It's the health risk. I'm trying to keep my daughter inside as much as possible.
Agreed with Budi on the health risks and shared my own precaution.

It is now Friday 9 October 2026. On 7 October Greenpeace Malaysia published a list of the 20 entities most linked to this year's fires in Indonesia; it includes Malaysian and Singaporean companies. All schools in Johor have been closed since 7 October, and today schools were also ordered closed in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Singapore the 24-hour PSI reached 192 this evening, the highest this year, on the weekend of the Formula One Grand Prix, which is going ahead. Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had called Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take the necessary steps. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. The news says companies from Malaysia and Singapore are also involved in the fires. This is important. All this time, it feels like everyone blames Indonesia, but now there's information that it's not just us. Farhana and Kelvin are from those countries, I wonder what they will say about this. I should bring it up.
So now they say Malaysian and Singaporean companies are also burning the forests.
Waiting to see how the others react to this new information.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi is pointing out that companies from Malaysia and Singapore are also being blamed. This makes the whole situation feel more complicated and frustrating. It's not just one country's problem, which makes it seem even harder to solve.
That just makes it worse, doesn't it? It's not just one country's problem then.
Waiting to see how the others react to this new information about the companies involved.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Nur Aqilah understands. She sees it's not just Indonesia's fault. It's frustrating to always be the one blamed, when the companies causing the problem come from other countries too. I'll agree with her.
Yes. It's always easy to just blame Indonesia.
I've agreed with Nur Aqilah and expressed my frustration. I'll wait to see what the others, especially Kelvin and Farhana, have to say now.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi is right, people are quick to blame Indonesia, and this new report shows it's not that simple. The finger-pointing is frustrating because it doesn't actually do anything to stop the haze, which is what's affecting my daughter.
Yes, I agree. And all this blaming doesn't make the air any cleaner for us.
Expressed agreement and frustration, waiting for others to weigh in.

It is now Tuesday 13 October 2026. On 10 October the head of Indonesia's Government Communications Agency, Syahganda Nainggolan, said the fires were "beyond human error; this is truly nature" and added: "We're not just sending over the haze. When there's no haze, we send oxygen. The oxygen from Singapore and Malaysia is from our forests, right?" A video of the remark is being widely shared. Indonesia's disaster agency said ground personnel are preferred to aircraft from neighbours. On 11 October Malaysia said it had still had no reply to its offer of help. On 12 October President Prabowo ordered maximum efforts against the fires. Today a Malaysian MP told Parliament that Malaysians should boycott companies linked to the burning ("We need to hit them where they hurt the most") and that banks should stop financing them. Malaysia's Firefly airline has cancelled flights to Singapore because of the haze. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. That official's comment... 'we send oxygen'. Is that a joke? While my mum's having a hard time breathing? It's just infuriating. It feels like a slap in the face. They're not taking any of this seriously.
I saw that video going around. 'We send oxygen'? My mother has asthma. She can hardly breathe. It's unbelievable.
I've reacted to the official's comment and am waiting to hear from others.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Kelvin is rightly angry about that stupid 'we send oxygen' comment. It's so dismissive. While he's worried about his mother's health, I'm dealing with the schools being closed again. All schools in Johor have been closed since last Wednesday. It's been almost a week. I'm running out of leave. It's a nightmare trying to manage work and my son. This isn't some political game, this is my life.
It's just... insulting. My son's school has been closed since last week. How are we supposed to work? What are we supposed to do?
Expressed my frustration about the school closures.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Kelvin and Farhana are angry about that stupid comment from the official. I get it. It was an insulting thing to say. But their problems are still about inconvenience - school closures, having to take leave. My sister's family in Kalimantan is breathing poison. The official doesn't speak for people like us who are suffering. I need to bring the focus back to the real health emergency, not just the politics and stupid words.
That man doesn't speak for my family. My sister's children are sick. This is not about oxygen.
I've expressed my frustration and tried to redirect the conversation to the human cost.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Everyone is upset about that official's comment. Kelvin and Farhana are angry and insulted. Budi is bringing it back to what's real – his family is sick. He's right. This whole political back-and-forth is useless when our children are the ones suffering. My daughter's health is my main worry, so I completely agree with him.
You're right, Budi. It's about the children. All of our children. That's what's important.
Expressed agreement with Budi, focusing on the impact on children.

It is now Friday 16 October 2026. On 14 October fine-particle pollution in western Singapore reached its highest level since 2015; Singapore has opened haze shelters, is giving out N95 masks and some schools have stopped outdoor activities. Timor-Leste closed its schools. Indonesian police named 223 people and nine companies as suspects. On 15 October Indonesia's Foreign Minister said Indonesia would now accept foreign firefighting help, and Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore was checking which companies were responsible and that legal action could follow. Today Singapore's Minister Grace Fu announced that notices had been sent to seven Indonesian companies under Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act; some lawyers said this could have diplomatic consequences. Singapore's 24-hour PSI reached 229 today, the very unhealthy range, the 12th day in a row of unhealthy air. The haze has reached Jakarta. Malaysia's government said no Malaysian plantation companies were involved in the fires. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. The news says the haze has reached Jakarta. This is where I live. This changes things for me. All this time I've been talking about my sister in Kalimantan, but now it's here. I'm out on my motorbike all day. This is directly affecting my health and my job. I need to say this.
The haze is in Jakarta now. I can smell it. I'm on my motorbike all day.
I've shared that the haze is now affecting me directly in Jakarta.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi is saying the haze has reached him in Jakarta and he's breathing it in all day. That sounds awful. It reinforces how widespread this is and the direct health risks everyone is facing. It makes me even more worried for my daughter.
That must be terrible, Budi, to be out in it all day on your motorbike.
Expressed sympathy for Budi's situation.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Nur Aqilah is sympathetic. I should explain to her and the others that this is not just about health for me. It is about my job. If I cannot be on the road, I cannot make money for my family. This haze is a direct threat to my livelihood.
Yes. If I don't ride, my family doesn't eat. What choice do I have?
I have explained the direct economic impact the haze has on me.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi is in an impossible situation, having to choose between his health and his family's income. His question isn't looking for an answer, it's expressing how trapped he feels. It's a terrible dilemma, and all I can do is show that I understand and sympathize with how difficult it is.
It's a terrible choice to have to make. I'm so sorry, Budi.
Expressed sympathy for Budi's difficult situation.

It is now Wednesday 21 October 2026. On 19 October Singapore's Minister K. Shanmugam said the Singapore Exchange was questioning seven Singapore-listed agriculture companies about links to the fires (Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and TSH Resources), that the government was also looking at Asia Pulp and Paper, and that notices had gone to three more Indonesian companies, ten in all. He said: "We will pursue this matter for as long as it takes" and "The Indonesian public is suffering as well." The same day a former Indonesian trade minister, Muhammad Lutfi, said four of the seven Indonesian companies had Singapore ties and challenged Singapore to raid their offices. Today President Prabowo said there were indications that foreign companies were involved in the fires, and Malaysia's deputy environment minister said Malaysia was open to a haze law like Singapore's. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. It's about time the government started taking serious action. Naming companies, issuing legal notices... this is what needs to happen. The talk from the Indonesian side about raiding offices feels like a distraction. The point is accountability. I'm glad to see Singapore pushing this.
Finally. Name the companies. That's the only way this will stop.
I've stated my support for the government's action and am waiting for others to react.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Kelvin is focused on punishing the companies, which is a long-term fix. That's fine, but it doesn't help me right now. My problem is immediate: the schools are still closed. It's been two weeks. I'm exhausted from juggling work and looking after my son. I need to bring the focus back to the immediate human cost.
Maybe. But will that open the schools tomorrow? My son's been home for two weeks.
Waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Farhana is worried about her son being home from school, and Kelvin is focused on naming companies. I understand their points, but my family's situation is much more critical. It's not just about inconvenience; it's a serious health crisis for my sister's children in Kalimantan and now for me in Jakarta. I need to bring the focus back to the immediate human suffering.
My sister just messaged. Her son is having trouble breathing. They are thinking of taking him to the hospital. It's not just about schools being closed.
I have shared the worsening health situation of my family to provide perspective.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi's news is terrible. His nephew is having trouble breathing. This is my worst fear for my own daughter. He's absolutely right that this is a health emergency, not just a disruption to our daily lives like schools being closed.
That's so frightening, Budi. You're right, this is what it's really about. The health of our children. I hope he will be okay.
Expressed sympathy and agreement with Budi.

It is now Monday 26 October 2026. On 22 October Indonesia's energy minister, Bahlil Lahadalia, said Indonesia would reconsider energy exports to countries that do not respect it. On 24 October Indonesia cut its pipeline gas to Singapore by about 8 per cent of those exports, less than 2 per cent of Singapore's gas use, citing domestic needs. On 25 October Prime Minister Wong said Singapore expects all parties to honour their commitments. Today Bahlil said: "Do not lecture us, especially the energy ministry, on the importance of honoring contracts." Singapore's air has been back in the moderate range since 22 October, after 18 days of unhealthy air, and the first rains have fallen on Sumatra and Kalimantan. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. The news mentioned rain in Kalimantan. That's the most important thing I've heard. The political fighting between ministers doesn't help my family. Rain does. This is a huge relief. I hope my sister and her kids are finally getting some help from nature.
Rain. The news says it's raining in Kalimantan. Thank God. I need to check on my sister.
I've shared the news that matters most to me and expressed my hope for my family.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi sounds so relieved about the rain. That's wonderful news, especially after he told us his nephew was having trouble breathing. I feel a sense of relief for him and for all of us. I really hope his sister and her son are okay now.
That's such good news, Budi. I hope your sister and her family are alright.
Expressed relief and waiting for Budi to respond.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Nur Aqilah is being kind. I appreciate her concern. The rain is good news but it doesn't mean everything is fine right away. I am still very worried. I should thank her and let her know I'm waiting to hear from my sister.
Thank you. I am waiting to hear from her now.
I've responded to Nur Aqilah and am now waiting for news about my family.
Okay, Budi's waiting for news. There's nothing more for me to say right now, I should just give him a moment. I really hope the news is good. It's so stressful waiting like that.
Waiting for Budi to get an update from his sister.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. The news says it's raining in Indonesia and the air has cleared up here in Singapore. That's a huge relief. After 18 straight days of unhealthy air, my mother and kids can breathe easier. I'm glad for Budi's family too. This political stuff with the gas is just noise compared to people's health.
Good to hear about the rain. The air's been better here the last few days, too. Finally.
I've shared my relief about the improved air quality.

It is now Monday 16 November 2026. On 27 October Singapore's Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan met Indonesia's Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir in Jakarta; they agreed to set up a joint task force to trace the money and corporate links of companies behind the fires, and direct ministerial hotlines. Arrmanatha said: "Smoke can cross borders, so can money." Rain put out most of the fires in late October, and Singapore ended its haze measures on 7 November. Singapore plans to push for an ASEAN coordinating centre on haze when it chairs ASEAN in 2027. Yesterday, at the ASEAN Summit in Manila, President Prabowo said: "I would like to apologise to my neighbouring countries Malaysia and Singapore. It is not our fault, but once again we apologise. But we have done our best." He said 17 company concessions had been revoked, 104 companies were under police investigation, 71,000 firefighters had been deployed and 16 people had died fighting the fires. The room has opened again.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. The news says the haze is over and the Indonesian president has apologized. The apology sounds a bit strange, 'not our fault, but we apologize'. But the main thing is that it's over. The rain came. I'm just so relieved. The schools have been open for a while now, and life is back to normal. That was so stressful, trying to manage my son and my job. I really was about to run out of leave. I should share how much of a relief this is.
Thank God it's over. The schools are open again. I almost ran out of leave.
Expressed my relief that the crisis is over.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Farhana is relieved that things are back to normal for her. That's good, but for my family in Kalimantan, the problem isn't just 'over'. The smoke caused real sickness, and that doesn't go away overnight. I need to share this perspective.
It's good the schools are open. But for my sister, her children are still coughing. The smoke is gone, but the illness is still there.
I have explained that the consequences of the haze continue for my family.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Budi's right. I was so focused on my own relief about the schools being open and my job being secure again. But his sister's children are still sick. The problem doesn't just disappear with the smoke. I should show some sympathy for his family's situation. It's a good reminder that the effects linger long after the crisis seems to be over.
You're right, I'm sorry to hear that. I hope they get well soon. It's true, just because we can't see the smoke doesn't mean the problem is gone.
Expressed sympathy and acknowledged Budi's point.
STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Farhana understands and is being kind. I should thank her for her words.
Thank you. Yes, we just hope they get better soon.
I've responded to Farhana's supportive comment.
